title: Su-34 Fullback (pilot)

sources.title: Su-27 DCS Flaming Cliffs Flight Manual EN (close sibling)
sources.file: Mods/aircraft/Su-27/Doc/Su-27 DCS Flaming Cliffs Flight Manual EN.pdf

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The Su-34 is a Russian two-seat strike aircraft developed from the Su-27. Its armoured cockpit is unusual: the pilot (left) and the navigator / weapons officer (right) sit side by side, and there is room behind the seats to stand, rest, heat food and use a toilet on long missions. The crew climbs in through the nose wheel bay. The grip functions are not public: JoyPro uses the Su-27 family set and marks it as assumed; the panels follow public descriptions.

areas.name: Head-up display
areas.text: The pilot's HUD and the keypad under it.

panels.name: Head-up display
panels.text: A wide-angle head-up display with a data entry panel below it.
panels.context: The pilot sits on the left; the HUD is in front of him.

controls.name: Head-up display (HUD)
controls.text: The glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes that shows flight numbers and aiming marks (head-up display). It shows speed, height, heading and the aiming marks for the weapons, so the pilot can read them while looking outside.
controls.context: The pilot keeps his eyes on it during take-off, landing and every attack, instead of looking down at the instruments.

controls.name: Up-front control panel
controls.text: A keypad with a small text display below the HUD, where the pilot types numbers such as radio frequencies and navigation points.
controls.context: Because it sits high up near the HUD, the pilot can enter data without looking far down into the cockpit. Its single switches are not described in the sources JoyPro uses.

areas.name: Multifunction displays
areas.text: The screens in front of both crew members.

panels.name: Multifunction displays
panels.text: Colour screens across the panel in front of both crew members, with standby instruments.
panels.context: Pilot and navigator sit side by side, so both can see the centre screen.

controls.name: Pilot MFDs
controls.text: The pilot's colour screen (a multi-function screen with buttons around its edge). It shows pages such as the flight data, the map and the weapons.
controls.context: The pilot chooses which page it shows; the same screen can show the radar, the map or the aircraft's systems.

controls.name: Centre MFD
controls.text: The middle colour screen (a multi-function screen with buttons around its edge). It shows pages that both crew members can see, such as the tactical situation.
controls.context: It sits between the two seats so pilot and navigator share one picture.

controls.name: Standby instruments
controls.text: Small backup instruments for attitude, speed and height. They keep working when the main screens or computers fail.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to fly safely home if the main displays are lost.

controls.name: Engine and fuel indicators
controls.text: Gauges that show how the two AL-31F-M1 engines run and how much fuel is left. They tell the pilot whether the engines are working normally.
controls.context: The pilot checks them during the engine start, before take-off and when something feels wrong.

areas.name: Navigator's station
areas.text: The navigator / weapons officer's seat on the right.

panels.name: Navigator's station
panels.text: The navigator / weapons officer sits on the right, side by side with the pilot, with his own screens and controls.
panels.context: He finds the way and the targets and works the weapons on long strike missions.

controls.name: Navigator MFDs
controls.text: The navigator's own colour screens for the navigation, the radar and the targeting systems.
controls.context: He watches the sensors here while the pilot flies.

controls.name: Data entry panel
controls.text: A keypad on the navigator's side for typing navigation and mission data.
controls.context: The single switches of the data entry panel are not described in the sources JoyPro uses.

controls.name: Weapon and sensor controls
controls.text: The navigator's controls for the sensors and the weapons.
controls.context: The single switches of the weapon and sensor controls are not described in the sources JoyPro uses.

areas.name: Rear space
areas.text: The space behind the seats for long missions.

panels.name: Rear space
panels.text: The armoured cockpit is roomy: behind the seats there is space to stand up, a small toilet, a food heater and room to rest. The crew enters through the nose wheel bay.
panels.context: Su-34 missions can last many hours, so the crew needs these comforts to stay fresh.

controls.name: Toilet
controls.text: A small toilet in the space behind the seats.
controls.context: It is rare in a fighter-sized aircraft and helps on very long flights.

controls.name: Galley (food heater)
controls.text: A small heater to warm up food on long missions.
controls.context: It lets the crew eat a warm meal in flight.

controls.name: Rest space
controls.text: Room behind the seats where a crew member can stand, stretch or rest.
controls.context: Moving around a little helps the crew stay alert on long missions.

panels.name: Control stick
panels.text: The centre stick of the Flanker family with the trim hat, the gun and stores triggers, the autopilot override lever and the target buttons.
panels.context: Su-34 grip functions are not public; JoyPro uses the Su-27 family set and marks it as assumed.

controls.name: Control stick
controls.text: The stick the pilot holds in his right hand. Pushing it forward lowers the nose, pulling it back raises the nose, and moving it left or right rolls the aircraft to that side. Computers between the stick and the control surfaces (fly-by-wire) turn these movements into commands.
controls.context: It is the main flight control; on most bindings it is the joystick's X and Y axes.

controls.name: Trim hat (TRIM)
controls.text: A small switch on top of the grip for the trim, small adjustments so the aircraft flies straight without the pilot holding the stick. Forward trims the nose down, back trims it up, left and right trim the roll.
controls.context: The pilot trims after every change of speed or configuration, so the stick feels light again.

controls.name: Gun trigger (OGON)
controls.text: The trigger at the front of the grip, under the index finger. Pulling it fires the GSh-30-1 cannon.
controls.context: It only fires when the weapons are armed with the master arm switch; the HUD or sight shows where the shots will go.

controls.name: Stores trigger (PODV)
controls.text: A flip-down trigger in front of the gun trigger. Pulling it launches the missiles or releases the bombs and other stores.
controls.context: On Flanker grips the gun and the stores have separate triggers, so the pilot cannot fire the wrong one by mistake. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

controls.name: Autopilot override trigger
controls.text: A lever low on the front of the grip. While the pilot holds it, the autopilot lets go and he can fly by hand; when he releases it, the autopilot takes over again.
controls.context: It is useful for a quick correction without switching the autopilot off. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

controls.name: Weapon select switch
controls.text: A switch on the grip head that steps through the weapon types.
controls.context: The pilot picks the next weapon without looking down. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

controls.name: Lock-on button
controls.text: Pressing this button locks the radar or sight onto the target.
controls.context: Once locked, the missiles get the target data they need. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

controls.name: Reset button (SBROS)
controls.text: Pressing this button breaks the lock and sends the radar back to searching.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to drop one target and look for another. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

controls.name: Nosewheel steering button
controls.text: While this button is held, the pilot steers the front wheel with the pedals on the ground (nosewheel steering, like a car's steering).
controls.context: It is used for taxiing. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.

panels.name: Throttles
panels.text: The two throttle levers for the two AL-31F-M1 engines, with the air brake switch, the target designator control and the countermeasures button.
panels.context: The catalog lists the throttles with the instrument panel, as they sit between the pilot and the panel in this side-by-side cockpit.

controls.name: Left throttle
controls.text: The left lever of the pair of throttles. It makes the left AL-31F-M1 engine stronger or weaker, like a car's gas pedal. Pushed fully forward it adds the afterburner for much more push.
controls.context: Both levers are normally moved together with one hand; they are split so each engine can be set alone, for example when one engine fails.

controls.name: Right throttle
controls.text: The right lever of the pair of throttles. It makes the right AL-31F-M1 engine stronger or weaker, like a car's gas pedal. Pushed fully forward it adds the afterburner for much more push.
controls.context: The pilot moves it together with the left lever; on a HOTAS with one throttle axis both engines can share the same axis.

controls.name: Air brake switch
controls.text: This switch opens and closes the airbrakes, panels that open into the wind to slow the aircraft down.
controls.context: The pilot opens them to lose speed quickly, for example before landing or to avoid flying past a target, and closes them to speed up again.

controls.name: Target designator control
controls.text: A tiny thumb joystick on the throttle grip that moves the target marker or the radar's scan zone on the screen. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to pick targets on the radar or sensor picture without taking his hand off the throttle.

controls.name: Countermeasures button
controls.text: Pressing this button throws out chaff (metal strips that confuse radar missiles) and flares (hot decoys for heat-seeking missiles).
controls.context: The pilot uses it when a missile is fired at him. Assumed from the Su-27 family; not confirmed for this aircraft.
